title: Retiam Engine: Bindless Varying Architecture & Performance Upgrades

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/BINDLESS_VARYING_STATE_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/BINDLESS_VARYING_STATE_ARCHITECTURE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.
This document details the architectural features, shader optimizations, bit-packing schemes, and pipeline fixes implemented in this development session for the **Retiam WebGPU Engine**.

cells.text: **Model & Raymarch Material Varying Optimization**
Fragment shaders were reading `(*_p_entity).material` from the global storage buffer, causing redundant GPU memory bus reads across millions of fragments.

Vertex shaders now pack PBR material properties into flat varyings (`v_mat_color`, `v_mat_em`, `v_mat_pbr`, `v_mat_tex`). Fragment shaders reconstruct `Material` in-register with **zero storage buffer memory reads**.
**Adaptive Dual-Mode Bit Packing (`packInstanceIndex`)**
50,000+ instances exceeded the previous 14-bit local instance boundary (16,384 instance limit) in `firstInstance`.

Implemented an adaptive MSB mode switch: Mode 0 (Standard: 18-bit state + 14-bit instance) and Mode 1 (Mega: 13-bit state + 18-bit instance up to 262,144 instances). Branchless WGSL decoding via `getStateIndex()` and `getLocalIndex()`.
**Programmable Storage Buffer Pulling**
WebGPU hardware vertex instancing (`stepMode: 'instance'`) calculates offset as `firstInstance * stride`. Using bit-packed MSB caused a 68 GB out-of-bounds fetch on vertex slot 1.
Replaced vertex buffer slot 1 instancing in `Instanced.ts` and `ModelGeometry.splat` with storage buffer pulling (`Res.storage('array<vec4f>', buffer)` at `@group(3)` binding 5).
**Volumetric SDF & 3D Raymarching Pipeline Fixes**
Custom raymarching domains threw `unresolved value 'state'` in WGSL when evaluating mathematical functions or user-defined `map(p)` routines referencing `state.t1` / `state.matrix`.
Added `var<private> state: State;` at WGSL module scope, synchronized `varyingSchema` with `v_mat_*` varyings, and properly bound `SDFParams` / `RMParams` uniforms.
**Destroyed Texture Bind Group Cache Invalidation**
When texture arrays were resized or re-allocated on the fly (e.g. font glyphs or materials loading), cached `@group(3)` instanced bind groups submitted destroyed texture views to the queue.
Added `_instancedAlbedoTex`, `_instancedNormalTex`, and `_instancedExtraBuffer` cache tracking in `RenderPass.ts`, automatically refreshing bind groups upon texture rebuilds.
**Zero-GC & Retained State Allocator Enhancements**
Per-frame allocations of `DrawCall[]`, `GeometryPassConfig`, and scene traversal states produced minor GC spikes on high entity counts.

Implemented persistent entity state slots (`acquireSlotForEntity` / `releaseSlot`), retained `_cachedDrawCalls` across geometries, cached `_cachedPasses`, and static pass-through traversal caching in `SceneComposer`.

blocks.text: Previously, during the rasterization of 3D Models, 3D SDF Volumes, and 3D Raymarched Surfaces, the fragment shader looked up the entity's material by executing:
For high-resolution framebuffers ($1920\times1080 = 2\text{M}$ pixels, or $4\text{K} = 8.3\text{M}$ pixels), every fragment evaluated executed a 96-byte global memory read from VRAM.
We eliminated fragment shader storage buffer reads by forwarding material data from the vertex shader:

blocks.code:
flowchart LR
    subgraph VertexStage [Vertex Shader]
        StateRead["Read states[getStateIndex(instance_index)]"] --> PackVaryings["Pack Material -> Varyings:
        v_mat_color: (color.rgb, opacity)
        v_mat_em: (emColor.rgb, emStrength)
        v_mat_pbr: (roughness, metallic, transmission, ior)
        v_mat_tex: (specular, albedoIdx, normalIdx, normalScale)"]
    end

    subgraph Rasterizer [Hardware Interpolator]
        PackVaryings --> Interp["@interpolate(flat) Varying Transfer"]
    end

    subgraph FragmentStage [Fragment Shader]
        Interp --> Unpack["Reconstruct struct Material from Varyings (Registers Only)"]
        Unpack --> PBR["PBR Lighting & Tone Mapping (Zero Storage Reads)"]
    end

blocks.text: Retiam packs both the **entity state index** and the **local instance / sub-element index** into WebGPU's 32-bit `firstInstance` parameter in `draw()` / `drawIndexed()`:

items: Normal scenes contain thousands of entities with few instances per entity.
Compute and swarm simulations contain a few entities with up to **262,144 instances** per entity.
**Bit 31**: Mode Switch (`0` = Standard Mode, `1` = Mega-Instance Mode)
**Bit 30 (`S`)**: Secondary Pass / Stroke Flag (`0` = Fill / Default, `1` = Stroke)

When `firstInstance` contained bit-packed metadata (such as `MSB = 1` $\rightarrow 2,147,745,792$), the GPU attempted to fetch vertex attributes from offset:
This resulted in WebGPU device validation failure: `Instance range requires a larger buffer than the bound buffer size`.
We migrated hardware vertex instancing to programmable storage pulling:

blocks.text: Mathematical raymarching formulas in `RaymarchPlot3D` and `SDFFragment` execute inside nested top-level WGSL helper functions (e.g. `map(p)`, `calcNormal(p)`, `surfaceFunc(x, z)`).

To give all nested functions access to the entity's current transform matrix, offsets, and dynamic time variables (`state.t1`, `state.t2`) without passing `State` through every function signature, we introduced **private module-scoped state**:
6. Texture Lifecycle & Dynamic Bind Group Cache Invalidation

When loading scenes with SDF fonts, images, or procedural textures, `Renderer.ts` dynamically reallocates `albedoTexArray` and `normalTexArray` to accommodate new texture layers, destroying the old $1024\times1024$ `rgba8unorm` texture array.
`RenderPass.ts` cached the `@group(3)` instanced bind group on the geometry:

blocks.code:
(packet.geometry as any)._instancedShadowBindGroup = instancedBindGroup;
(packet.geometry as any)._instancedBufferVersion = (packet.geometry as any).version;

blocks.text: Because `geometry.version` did not change when the texture array rebuilt, the draw call submitted the stale bind group referencing the **destroyed** texture.
We expanded the cache invalidation condition to monitor texture identity and extra buffer pointers:

children: Entities retain a stable slot in `GlobalStateAllocator` via `acquireSlotForEntity(entity)` / `releaseSlot(slot)`.
Bypasses repeated allocation/free cycles across frames.

`ModelGeometry`, `MorphGeometry`, `TextGeometry`, and `TriangulatedPathGeometry` use fixed retained `DrawCall[]` arrays (`_cachedDrawCalls`) updated in-place instead of instantiating new arrays every frame.
Geometries cache their `Record<string, GeometryPassConfig>` dictionaries in `_cachedPasses`, eliminating per-frame object allocation during render queue construction.

Integrated with [`RenderStateCache.setScissorRect`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/RenderStateCache.ts), skipping redundant WebGPU scissor commands across batches.
